description: User directed 2026-11-19: "add the elixir parity issues as tickets to the epic we gave to Elixir Parity". Owner: Elixir Parity. After a FunctionClauseError, catch kind, reason binds %FunctionClauseError{} in fz; Elixir's catch normalisation binds the raw :function_clause. Done: catch sees what Elixir's sees, on three paths.

comments.text: HOLD (2026-11-24, relayed by Elixir Parity): the user is reconsidering the whole approach — raise structs natively, convert only at a catch that reads the reason. Nothing mue.28-related proceeds until decided.

User decision 2026-11-24 (in Elixir Parity's session): "let's go with the cheaper shape". fz raises exception structs natively for its own errors, as before this ticket. rescue converts only raw terms a program raised itself (:erlang.error(term)). A catch clause that binds or tests the reason translates fz's runtime-error structs back to Elixir's Erlang reasons (%FunctionClauseError{} -> :function_clause, %MatchError{term: t} -> {:badmatch, t}, ...); a catch _, _ costs nothing. Known deviation, to be tracked in its own ticket: a user-raised ArgumentError and fz's own :badarg look the same to a catch that reads the reason. This replaces the reason-raising design and the page ../fz-mue.28.html (rescue as Elixir compiles it).

User decision 2026-11-24: go with the cheaper shape. fz's runtime keeps raising exception structs. rescue converts only raw terms the program itself raises (:erlang.error(term)), and only when the raised type contains any. A catch clause that binds or tests the reason translates the struct back to Elixir's Erlang reason; a catch written _, _ costs nothing. Known deviation: a catch that reads the reason can't tell a struct fz's runtime raised (Elixir would show a raw reason) from the same struct raised explicitly by the program. The earlier approach (raise Erlang reasons, normalize on every rescue: +212 derivations / +1880 reads / +272 requests at 15936097f) is attached as fz-mue.28-raise-reasons-normalize-on-rescue.patch (4 WIP commits, base merge-base of 35b26559c), kept at the user's request.
